title: Build a vowel and take it apart with LPC
brief: Synthesize vowels from an impulse train and formant resonators, then recover the formants with Levinson-Durbin LPC and the pitch with the real cepstrum.
hints: In levinson_durbin, the update for step i reads the previous coefficients in reverse: alpha_j <- alpha_j - k_i * alpha_{i-j}. Copy the old array before you overwrite it.
The numerator of step i is r[i] - sum_{j=1}^{i-1} alpha_j r[i - j]; with 0-based arrays, that is r[i] - alpha[:i-1] @ r[i-1:0:-1].
A(z) has coefficients [1, -alpha_1, ..., -alpha_p]. np.fft.rfft(those, n_fft) evaluates it on the rfft grid, and np.roots(those) gives its roots.
Every real polynomial's complex roots come in conjugate pairs. Keep only np.imag(root) > 0, so each formant appears once.
The cepstrum's pitch peak sits at the period in samples, sample_rate / F0: 133 samples for 120 Hz at 16 kHz.
